one_liner: Vonage offers self-serve credentials and public APIs for messaging, voice, numbers, applications, and account management.

auth.notes: Vonage recommends JWT authentication for most Messages API use cases; this is not a documented user-delegated OAuth flow. SIP Trunking uses Digest authentication. Authentication varies by product.

access.notes: Cloud signup provides an API key and secret and initial free credit without a credit card. API usage is charged per request, and developers can top up when credit runs low.

api.notes: The public reference covers communications and account-management APIs; the getting-started guide describes Curl requests and OpenAPI specifications.

mcp.notes: Vonage documents a Tooling MCP Server that invokes API actions.

verdict.rationale: Self-serve signup yields API credentials and initial free credit. Public documentation covers communications, numbers, and application-management actions; API usage is charged per request.

evidence.quote: When you create a Vonage account, an API key and secret will be created for you. These are located in your account settings in the Vonage Dashboard.
A number of newer Vonage APIs require authentication to be done using an API key and secret sent Base64 encoded in the Authorization header.
Messages supports both JWT and Basic authentication, however basic authentication does not support webhooks or advanced features such as ACLs. For most use-cases we recommend JWT Authentication.
SIP Trunking uses Digest Authentication method with the API Key as user and API Secret as password.
To work with our APIs, you will need to sign up for an account . This will give you an API key and secret that you can use to access our APIs.
Start developing now with free credit. No credit card required.
Access to our APIs is charged on a per-request basis. We’ll give you some free credit when you first open your account and you can top up when you run low.

When our APIs want to notify your app about something - whether that is an inbound call or message or a status update - they require your app to expose a URL endpoint that our platform can make a request to.
If you are familiar with the command-line tool Curl , you will find Curl snippets for each of our APIs that you can copy, paste and modify.
Each of our APIs has its own OpenAPI specification . You can read more about OpenAPI in our documentation .
The Voice API lets you dial other phones, answer incoming calls, and control all aspects of the call including conferences, recordings, capturing user input and sending various audio content.
Manage all the numbers you need for your applications. Search for numbers, list and configure your purchased numbers, cancel any number you no longer need.
The Vonage Server API Bindings MCP Server , also known as the Tooling MCP Server, lets you invoke various API actions directly through your LLM Assistant or IDE of choice.
The MCP extension will automatically download and start the Vonage Tooling MCP Server .
This will give you an API key and secret that you can use to access our APIs.
Create and manage the applications you use across Vonage APIs. Create, manage and configure your applications and authentication.

problems: Individual API-reference pages fetched for SMS and applications exposed only a page shell; the API index and getting-started guide were readable.
The Composio toolkit URL could not be read directly; extraction reported a 404. No quoted evidence establishes its catalog status.
The cited authentication guidance recommends JWTs for Messages API use cases, not a single authentication method for every Vonage product.
name: Vonage

verification.note: Quotes show an account API key and secret, Basic auth (key/secret Base64 in the Authorization header, and Messages Basic), JWT (bearer token you mint; recommended for most Messages use cases), and SIP Digest (other). Nothing recommends a different primary. The note’s claim that there is no user-delegated OAuth flow is not in the quotes.
Signup yields an API key and secret; free credit is given with no credit card, and usage is then charged per request with top-up. That is self-serve credentials with no payment or approval.
Public pages describe Curl calls and per-API OpenAPI specs plus write actions for voice, numbers, and applications. Breadth broad is an estimate and is not contradicted.
Vonage’s own developer docs describe the Tooling MCP Server as downloadable and startable and able to invoke API actions. Nothing labels it beta, pilot, or unreleased.
No claim was made, so there is nothing to check.
Self-serve free credentials plus a documented, non-read-only public API meet buildable_now with main_blocker none. Per-request charging after free credit is noted and does not change that.
